glosses: To fall heavily due to lack of energy.

examples.text: He flopped down in front of the television, exhausted from work.

There was [in the clock in Lyons Cathedral] a centre puppet of the Virgin Mary; and close to her, a small pigeon-hole, out of which another and a very ill-looking puppet made one of the most sudden plunges I ever saw accomplished: instantly flopping back again at sight of her, and banging his little door violently, after him.

glosses: To cause to drop heavily.

examples.text: The tired mule flopped its ears forward and trudged on.

glosses: To fail completely; not to be successful at all (of a movie, play, book, song etc.).

examples.text: The latest album flopped and so the studio canceled her contract.

glosses: To pretend to be fouled in sports, such as basketball, hockey (the same as to dive in soccer)

examples.text: It starts with Chris Paul, because Blake didn't really used to flop like that, you know, last year.
While Stern chastised Vogel for on Thursday calling the Heat "the biggest flopping team in the NBA," he did intimate that he sees merit in the sentiment.

glosses: To strike about with something broad and flat, as a fish with its tail, or a bird with its wings; to rise and fall; to flap.

examples.text: The brim of a hat flops.

glosses: To have (a hand) using the community cards dealt on the flop.

examples.text: Both players flopped sets! Cards dealt on the flop: Q95. Player A's hole cards: 55 (making three of a kind: 555). Player B's hole cards: QQ (making three of a kind: QQQ).

glosses: To stay, sleep or live in a place.

examples.text: […] not just the old material goal of "three hots and a place to flop," […]
They have opened up crypts and basements as immense pads where vagrant and impoverished hippies can flop for the night.

glosses: To flip; to reverse (an image).

examples.text: […] in order to flop the image left-to-right, or all printing will appear reversed.
The possibilities of this type of shot are almost limitless. By quartering the screen and duplicating and flopping the picture, a kaleidoscopic effect is achieved.

glosses: To deny someone parole.

examples.text: I've been incarcerated going on 9½ years. I have never been back on the streets or given a chance to prove myself to society. Every time I would meet the parole board they would flop me telling me I would be a threat to society.

glosses: A heavy, passive fall; a plopping down.

examples.text: The gigaflop supercomputers of today are almost useless. What is needed is a teraflop machine. That’s a machine that can run at a trillion flops, a trillion floating-point operations per second, or roughly a thousand times as fast as Cray Y-MP8.

examples.text: He sat with an unenthusiastic slouch.

examples.text: In any case, Scotland has been no slouch at national invention. examples.text: […] then he slouched his head down on the table and pretended to sleep.

examples.text: Comme si le peuple était un vil troupeau d’esclaves stupidement attaché au stupide tyran qu’il a proscrit, voulant, à quelque prix que ce soit, se vautrer dans la bassesse et dans la servitude.
